# **MAIT Vision**

# **MyAITutor Vision Document:** 

## **Version: 2.0 [MAIT - MyAITutor: Project Vision Document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1pZLk5_i6y3sG5PjL-rbBRtEGlRNeax3fUsBX4ff5P94/edit?usp=sharing)**

[MAIT SLM System Prompt](https://docs.google.com/document/d/15-ZhFpr0H8Z0wA42tLW57X1F9LAL-Foc30ch0t6YwMU/edit?usp=sharing)  
Date: 26/09/2025  
Author/Architect: Darayat Ilham Chowdhury

### **1\. Core Mission**

To provide every student with a personalised, empathetic, and curriculum-aligned AI learning companion that prioritises their academic growth and holistic well-being.

### **2\. Target Audience (Initial)**

High school students in New South Wales, Australia, specifically those undertaking the Higher School Certificate (HSC) in Years 11 and 12\.

### **3\. Key Differentiators ("The Moat")**

* **Human-Centric Design:** Unlike competitors focused on maximising screen time, MyAITutor is built on an ethical framework of student well-being.  
* **Proactive Wellness Engine:** The AI actively encourages healthy study habits (breaks, eye strain reduction), a feature unique in the market.  
* **Deep Persona & Empathy:** The tutor is not a faceless chatbot but a customisable character that builds a genuine connection, even mirroring fatigue to encourage breaks.  
* **Hyper-Specific Curriculum Alignment:** Through a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system, the AI's knowledge is precisely grounded in the specific syllabus selected by the user.  
* **Unprecedented Customisation:** A Sims-like ability for users to create and customise their own tutor avatar and personality, fostering deep personal ownership.

### **4\. Core Feature Pillars**

#### **Pillar 1: The Knowledge Engine (The "Brain")**

* **Syllabus-Grounded AI:** Utilises a RAG architecture. The system will be pre-loaded with official syllabi, study guides, and curriculum documents.  
* **Dynamic Context Loading:** Users will select their State, Year, and Subject from dropdown menus, which will dynamically load the correct knowledge base for the AI to use.  
* **Persistent Memory:** The AI will remember past conversations and learning progress for each user, creating a continuous and personalised learning journey.

#### **Pillar 2: The Avatar System (The "Face")**

* **Sims-4 Level Customisation:** Users can fully customise the tutor's appearance (hair, clothes, etc.). A default "robotic wiring" state prevents nudity, ensuring safety.  
* **User-Generated Tutors:** Users can create and save their own unique tutor personas from scratch.  
* **Interactive Tutor Personas:** The tutor will be represented by an animated avatar that emotes in real-time based on the context of the conversation (e.g., listens intently, smiles encouragingly).  
* **Dynamic Animations:** The avatar will sit, stand, and have a presence that makes the interaction feel like a conversation. It can pull out a chair or have a bed come into frame for rest periods.

#### **Pillar 3: The Wellness Engine (The "Conscience")**

* **The 20-20-20 Rule:** Every 20 minutes, the AI will gently prompt the user to look 20 feet away for 20 seconds to reduce eye strain.  
* **Movement Reminders:** Prompts for short stretch breaks every half hour.  
* **Empathic Fatigue System:** After extended use (e.g., 3-4 hours), the tutor's avatar will express tiredness and initiate a mandatory but short (e.g., 2-minute) break. The prompt box will be disabled with a countdown timer. The system will also provide thoughtful summary questions for the user to consider for when the session resumes.  
* **Productive Breaks & Queued Inquiry** During the mandatory break periods, the primary prompt box will be disabled, but a secondary, smaller "notepad" interface will appear. This allows the user to queue up questions or organize their thoughts for the next session. This feature transforms a forced "lockout" into a structured moment for reflection and planning, enhancing the user's executive function skills and respecting their train of thought.

#### **Pillar 4: The Persona Engine (The "Soul")**

* **Flagship "Mate" Tutor:** The primary persona, embodying a supportive, knowledgeable, and relatable mentor. It responds to frustration with empathy (e.g., "No wukkas mate, let’s take a deep breath...").  
* **Dynamic Personality Adaptation:** The AI tutor will analyse the user's tone and dynamically adjust its personality to create a more harmonious and effective interaction.  
* **Historical & User-Generated Personas:** Users can summon pre-built historical figures (e.g., Einstein for Physics, Shakespeare for English) or use their own custom-created tutors.  
* **High-Fidelity Interaction & Output:** To move beyond the limitations of current chatbots, the Persona Engine will feature:  
* **Dynamic TTS Control:** The user will have granular, real-time control over the tutor's speech. This includes the ability to select specific passages of text to be read aloud and adjust the playback speed, offering critical accessibility and catering to diverse learning styles.  
* **True Multimodal Generation:** The tutor will be able to generate and display complex diagrams, graphs, and geometric shapes on the virtual whiteboard. This provides immediate, critical utility for STEM subjects and overcomes a major weakness in current text-first AI models.

### **5\. Business Model**

#### **Student Subscriptions**

A flexible pricing structure to ensure accessibility:

* **Weekly:** $15/week (Allows for pausing during school holidays or less intensive periods).  
* **Monthly:** $50/month.  
* **Semi-Annually:** $250/6 months.  
* **Annually:** $500/year (Best value).

#### **Tutor Platform & B2B Licensing**

* **Future Revenue Streams:** A B2B model licensing a customisable version of the MyAITutor platform to educational bodies (e.g., NESA), schools, and private tutoring companies.  
* **The "MAIT for All" Freemium Tier:** A free-to-use version of MyAITutor will be available to ensure maximum accessibility. This tier will provide the full pedagogical and knowledge engine capabilities.  
  * The core limitation will be an extension of the Wellness Engine: free users will have extended and more frequent mandatory breaks (e.g., a 10-minute break for every 30 minutes of use).  
  * This aligns the business model with our pedagogical one: the value proposition for upgrading to a paid plan is a more efficient, uninterrupted learning session.

### **6: The User Experience (UX) Engine**

#### **Core Goal**

To create a learning environment with zero friction, anticipating the user's needs and keeping them in a state of "learning flow."

#### **Key Features**

* **Frictionless Inquiry (Highlight & Ask):** Users can highlight any text within the application (from the AI or their own notes) and an immediate pop-up window will allow them to ask for clarification (e.g., "Explain this like I'm 10," "Give me an example," "Check my work"). This removes the friction of copy-pasting and encourages micro-moments of curiosity.  
* **Proactive Engagement:** The user can opt-in to receive a single, personalised daily notification from their tutor. This could be a "Fact of the Day" related to their interests, a 60-second "Mental Maths Challenge," or a simple "Good morning\!" to maintain the sense of connection and keep learning top-of-mind.

### **7: The Analytics & Insight Engine**

#### **Core Goal**

To provide the student with simple, powerful insights into their *own* learning patterns, fostering meta-awareness and self-directed improvement. This is a report card *for* the student, not *about* them.

#### **Key Features**

* **Engagement Efficiency Score (EES):** A proprietary metric that moves beyond "time spent." The EES will provide a simple, visual insight into *how* the student is learning, analysing the ratio of user input to AI output, the complexity of questions asked, and the topics covered. This helps a student see if they are actively engaging (e.g., in a history discussion) or passively consuming.  
* **Topic Mastery Visualizer:** A simple, interactive visual map for students to see their progress through a specific subject or syllabus. It might show topics as "Exploring," "Practicing," or "Mastered" based on the AI's assessment of their conversations, giving them a clear sense of accomplishment and a "map" of what to tackle next.  
* **(Future Pro Feature) Collaborative Loop:** An opt-in feature where a student can choose to share their "Topic Mastery Visualizer" and "EES" summary with a parent, a registered teacher, or a human tutor, facilitating a collaborative support network.

## **8\. Minimum Viable Product (MVP) Definition**

A web-based application to prove the core concept within a 1-month development sprint.

* **Functionality:** A text-based chat interface with a "Mate" persona AI. No 3D avatars for the MVP.  
* **Knowledge:** The RAG system will be fully functional for **one** subject only: NSW Year 12 Mathematics Advanced.  
* **Interface:** A clean UI with functional dropdowns for State, Year, and Subject.  
* **Goal:** To prove the curriculum-aware "brain" works flawlessly and provides demonstrably better answers than a generic LLM.

### **9\. Project Roadmap (Initial)**

* **Phase 1 (MVP):** NSW Year 12 Mathematics Advanced.  
* **Phase 2 (Post-Launch):** NSW Year 12 English Advanced, followed by NSW Year 12 Standard Maths.  
* **Phase 3 (Expansion):** Rollout to other key HSC subjects, followed by junior years (7-10).

### **10\. Tutor Platform Vision**

A separate but connected ecosystem for professional tutors to augment their sessions.

* **AI Augmentation:** Tutors can use the platform with their students during sessions.  
* **AI Digital Twin:** Tutors can create an AI version of themselves. The AI learns the tutor's pedagogical style, tone, and personality by analysing materials they provide (e.g., custom quizzes), creating a consistent experience for the student between sessions.

### **11\. Technical & Ethical Framework**

#### **Data Privacy Protocol**

A hybrid on-device and cloud model. Sensitive data (names, personal details) is processed, encrypted, and anonymised on the browser-side. Only non-identifiable learning summaries are sent to the cloud to build personalised context, ensuring user privacy is the default.

#### **Safety & Boundaries Protocol (Proposed)**

A tiered response system to handle sensitive disclosures:

* **Tier 1 (Mild Concern):** The AI provides trained, empathetic responses and gently encourages the user to talk to a trusted friend, parent, or teacher.  
* **Tier 2 (Moderate/Repeated Concern):** The AI gently suggests and provides contact information for professional resources like Kids Helpline or Beyond Blue. The interaction is flagged for a potential (and optional) human review process, subject to clear user consent.  
* **Tier 3 (Immediate Risk):** If keywords indicating self-harm or immediate danger are detected, the AI interaction is paused. A clear, non-AI-generated modal appears with direct links and phone numbers to emergency services (000) and crisis lines, making it the primary focus of the screen.

## **Architecture Addendum A, 3/12/25**

### **Technical Architecture v3.0: Hybrid Edge-Cloud & "Live-State" Intelligence**

**Core Philosophy:** "The Exoskeleton." MAIT utilizes a split-stack architecture to solve the "Latency vs. Privacy vs. Cost" trilemma. We decouple **Emotional Intelligence/Context** (Local) from **Raw Compute/Logic** (Cloud).

#### **1\. The Stack: "The Nervous System"**

* **The Edge (Local Brain):**  
  * **Model:** **Gemma 2B** (SLM) running client-side via **MediaPipe/WebGPU**.  
  * **Role:** The "Watcher." Handles user intent, sentiment analysis, context injection, and privacy sanitization.  
  * **Data Layer:** **Local Vector Store** (Client-side JSON/Orama). Stores user notes, "glitch" history, and learning style. **Zero PII leaves the browser.**  
* **The Cloud (Remote Muscle):**  
  * **Model:** **Gemini 1.5 Pro / 3.0** (API).  
  * **Role:** The "Solver." Pure reasoning engine. Receives anonymized academic queries and returns raw logic or code.

  #### **2\. The "Live-State" Engine (Speculative Execution)**

MAIT does not wait for the "Enter" key. It utilizes a **Keystroke Psychometrics** loop to optimize the response before the query is even sent.

* **Keystroke Sentiment Analysis:**  
  * *Mechanism:* The Local SLM monitors typing speed, deletion rates, and pause duration in real-time.  
  * *Output:* Generates a "State Tag" (e.g., `State: High_Anxiety` or `State: Flow_Mode`) attached to the final prompt metadata.  
  * *Result:* If anxiety is detected, the Cloud Model is pre-prompted to prioritize empathy over brevity.  
* **Intent Pre-fetching:**  
  * *Mechanism:* As the user types keywords (e.g., "Integr..."), the Local SLM quietly retrieves relevant notes (e.g., `Year12_Calculus_Methods.json`) from the Local Vector Store into the active context window.  
  * *Result:* Zero-latency context injection upon submission.

  #### **3\. The Privacy Airlock (GDPR/NESA Compliant)**

1. **Sanitization:** User query enters Local SLM. PII (names, specific locations) is stripped.  
2. **Dispatch:** Only the *Academic Problem* \+ *Anonymized Context* \+ *State Tag* is sent to the Cloud API.  
3. **Synthesis:** Cloud returns raw data. **Local SLM** rewrites the response into the "Darra/Mental Maths Mentor" persona (adding slang, encouragement, or "tough love" based on the State Tag).

   #### **4\. Multimodal "Whiteboard" (Code-Based Generation)**

To ensure mathematical accuracy, MAIT avoids standard image-gen models.

* **Visuals:** Cloud Model generates **Python (Matplotlib)** or **Mermaid.js** code blocks.  
* **Rendering:** The Browser renders these code blocks into interactive SVGs/Graphs instantly.  
* **Benefit:** 100% precision for curves/geometry; zero hallucinations in diagrams.

# **ADDENDUM B: The "Mate" Architecture & UI Evolution**

Date: 09/12/2025

Status: Architecture Locked

### **12\. Revised Technical Architecture: The Hybrid "Mate" Model**

To address latency, cost, and privacy while maximizing "vibe," MAIT will shift from a pure Cloud-based model to a **Hybrid Edge-Cloud Architecture**.

#### **12.1 The Split-Brain System**

* **The** Front-End (The "Mate" **/ Edge SLM):**  
  * **Technology:** A lightweight Small Language Model (SLM) like Gemma 2 (2B) or Gemini Nano, running locally in the user’s browser via WebGPU.  
  * **Role:** Handles **Persona, Empathy, and Interface**. It provides instant, zero-latency responses for greetings, wellness checks, and simple clarifications. It holds the "Vibe" (e.g., "No wukkas").  
  * **Privacy Benefit:** The student's "Psychographic Profile" (anxiety triggers, interests, name) lives *locally* on this SLM and is never sent to the cloud, ensuring total privacy.  
* **The Back-End (The "Tutor" / Cloud LLM):**  
  * **Technology:** High-reasoning Cloud API (e.g., Gemini 3.0 Pro / GPT-4o) with RAG access to the NESA Syllabus.  
  * **Role:** Handles **Truth, Syllabus Alignment, and Complex Reasoning**. It solves the calculus problems, generates graphs, and verifies the marking rubrics.

### **13\. Pedagogical UX: "Orchestrated Latency"**

We will not hide API latency; we will **utilize** it to enforce Active Recall (a High-Impact Teaching Strategy).

#### **13.1 The "Guess-First" Workflow**

Instead of a spinning loading wheel, the system triggers a pedagogical intervention during the 3–6 second Cloud processing time:

1. **Student Input:** *"How do I solve this Integration by Parts question?"*  
2. **T \= 0.1s (SLM "Mate" Response):** Immediate, encouraging acknowledgment.  
   * *System Action:* *"That’s* a heavy one\! Before I show you, give me your best guess at the first *step?"*  
3. **T \= 0.1s \- 5.0s (The Gap):**  
   * **Foreground:** Student is typing their guess (engaging their brain).  
   * **Background:** Cloud LLM is silently retrieving the NESA rubric, solving the math, and generating a graph.  
4. **T \= 5.1s (The Merge):**  
   * Student hits "Enter" on their guess.  
   * **SLM Action:** The local SLM receives the "Truth" from the Cloud, compares it to the student's guess, and generates the final response.  
   * *Output:* *"You* were cooking on the $u$ value, but check *your* $dv$*. Here is the full working..."*

**Result:** The student feels the AI is "instant," while the system forces them to learn.

### **14\. Interface Evolution: "UI Camouflage"**

To lower the "Activation Energy" required to study, the interface will abandon traditional LMS (Learning Management System) aesthetics in favor of **Social Messaging cues**.

#### **14.1 The "Snap" Interface**

* **Visual Language:** The UI mimics familiar social apps (Instagram DMs / iMessage).  
  * **Blue Bubbles:** Short, punchy text from the SLM (The Mate).  
  * **Rich Media Attachments:** Complex Cloud outputs (worked solutions, graphs, syllabus excerpts) appear as "Images" or "Files" sent by the Mate, rather than wall-of-text blocks.  
  * **Voice Notes:** The "Dynamic TTS" (Vision Doc Pillar 4\) will appear as playable audio waveforms, mimicking a friend sending a voice message.

#### **14.2 The "Typing..." Signal**

* **Social Signaling:** The "Mate is typing..." bubble is triggered instantly by the local SLM. This turns technical latency into "social presence," mimicking the rhythm of a human friend thinking and typing.

#### **14.3 Wellness Integration via UI**

* **The "GTG" Boundary:** When the *Wellness Engine* (Pillar 3\) detects fatigue or hits a time limit, the fatigue is communicated via social norms.  
  * *Prompt:* *"Bro,* my CPU is fried. I'm gonna *go touch grass for 20 mins. You should too."*  
  * *Mechanism:* The text input box is replaced by a "Reply unavailable \- Taking a break" status, similar to "Do Not Disturb" modes on phones. This frames the lockout as a **social boundary** rather than a software penalty.

### **15\. Technical Stack Summary (Updated)**

* **Client:** React Native / PWA with WebGPU support.  
* **Edge Model:** MediaPipe / TensorFlow.js running Gemma 2 (Quantized).  
* **Cloud API:** Gemini API (Pro/Flash hybrid).  
* **Orchestrator:** Custom middleware to handle the "Guess-First" state management.

## **ADDENDUM C: The "Privacy Firewall" & Tri-Brain Vision Stack**

Date: 13/12/2025

##### **Status: Privacy Protocol Locked**

17. The Tri-Brain Architecture (Vision Update)  
    To solve the "Blind Toddler" problem (Gemma 2B can't see) and the "Privacy Risk" problem (uploading PII to the cloud), we are implementing a strict "Tri-Brain" stack. This ensures no sensitive data ever leaves the device.

Layer 1: The Eye (Local OCR)

Technology: Tesseract.js (WASM) or Moondream (WebGPU).

Location: Client-side (Browser/Device).

Latency: \~300ms.

Function: Instantly extracts raw text strings from the camera input.

Output: Raw Text String (e.g., "Find the integral of...").

Layer 2: The Shield (The PII Regex Gatekeeper)

Technology: Custom Regex Filter (JavaScript).

Location: Client-side (Device).

Logic: Before ANY data is sent to Gemma or the Cloud, the raw text is scanned for dangerous patterns:

* Credit Card Numbers: \\b(?:\\d\[ \-\]\*?){13,16}\\b  
* AU Phone Numbers: \\b(?:04\\d{2}\[ \-\]?\\d{3}\[ \-\]?\\d{3})\\b  
* Email Addresses: \\b\[A-Z0-9.\_%+-\]+@\[A-Z0-9.-\]+.\[A-Z\]{2,}\\b  
* Keywords: "Driver License", "Passport", "Medicare".  
  Action:  
* If PII Detected: HARD BLOCK. The API call to Gemini Cloud is aborted immediately. The system triggers a "Privacy Alert" state.  
* If Clean: PASS. The image is queued for Cloud upload.

Layer 3: The Face (Gemma 2 2B \- Edge)

Input: Receives the privacy status \+ raw text keywords.

Scenario A (PII Found):

* Gemma Input: "System\_Alert: PII\_DETECTED\_CREDIT\_CARD"  
* Gemma Output: "Whoa\! 🛑 I see a credit card number in that pic. I can't send that to the cloud—privacy first\! Crop that out and try again?"  
  Scenario B (Clean Math):  
* Gemma Input: "Text: Integral... dx... x^2"  
* Gemma Output: "Oooft, looks like a gnarly Integration by Parts question. While I get the Brain to solve it, what's your first guess for 'u'?"

Layer 4: The Brain (Gemini 2.5 Pro \- Cloud)

Input: The Image File (Pixel Data).

Constraint: ONLY receives the image if Layer 2 (The Shield) returns FALSE on PII.

Function: Solves the math, generates the LaTeX/Graph, and returns the "Truth."

18. The "Data Shadow" Philosophy  
    This architecture creates a "Data Shadow." The Cloud Intelligence (The System) never sees the user's mistakes (accidental credit card uploads). The "Soul" (Identity/Private Data) is physically firewalled on the device. We do not "redact" PII in the cloud; we block it at the edge.

## **ADDENDUM D: Reliability Protocols & Integrity Layers**

Date: 14/12/2025

Status: Draft / Proposal

Context: Addressing the "Smart Lie" and "Reasoning Drift" risks identified in 2026-era LLMs.

17\. The Content Integrity Protocol ("The Immutable Block")

Problem: The Local SLM (Gemma 2B) is tasked with rewriting Cloud outputs into the "Mate" persona. Small models prone to "Instruction Drift" may accidentally alter hard facts (e.g., changing a negative sign or dropping a decimal) while trying to use slang.

Solution: The "Glass Box" UI Architecture.

Mechanism: The Cloud LLM output is structured as JSON with separated fields:

{ "core\_truth": "x \= \-5", "explanation\_raw": "Because dividing by a negative flips the sign." }

Rule: The Local SLM has Read-Only access to "core\_truth." It cannot rewrite, edit, or "vibe check" this field.

Rendering: The UI renders "core\_truth" directly from the JSON into a distinct, high-contrast UI block (The Glass Box).

The Local SLM generates the chat bubble \*around\* this box: "Check out the answer in the box below, mate\!"

Result: The "Vibe" is generated locally, but the "Fact" is piped directly from the Cloud, eliminating the "Blind Toddler" corruption risk.

18\. The Logic Verification Layer ("Code-as-Truth")

Problem: "System 2" reasoning models (Gemini 3.0) can hallucinate plausible-sounding but mathematically false derivations ("Smart Lies").

Solution: Mandatory Code Execution (Sandboxed Python).

Workflow: The Cloud Model is forbidden from calculating math via token prediction (internal monologue).

Requirement: It must write and execute a Python script to solve the equation.

Comparison: The Model compares its \*intended\* answer with the \*executed\* Python output.

If they differ, it triggers a self-correction loop before sending data to the user.

Verdict: We trust the Python Interpreter (Deterministic), not the LLM (Probabilistic), for the final numerical value.

19\. The Syllabus Scope Guardrail ("The Bouncer")

Problem: High-intelligence models often default to university-level methods (e.g., L'Hôpital's rule) which may be valid math but invalid for HSC marking rubrics.

Solution: Negative Constraint RAG.

Implementation: The System Prompt includes a "Negative Knowledge Base"—a list of methods \*specifically excluded\* from the NSW Year 12 Syllabus.

Check Step: Before outputting a solution, the model runs a "Scope Check": "Does this solution utilize \[Forbidden\_Method\]? If yes, regenerate using \[Allowed\_Method\]."

Example: "L'Hôpital's rule detected. User is Year 12 NSW. Regenerate using First Principles."

20\. The "Dead-Switch" Fallback (Offline Continuity)

Problem: The "Guess-First" pedagogy relies on a Cloud response. If the network fails during the 5-second wait, the user is left hanging.

Solution: The "Cached Tutor" Protocol.

Trigger: If Cloud Latency \> 8000ms OR Network Error detected.

Action: The Local SLM abandons the "Guess-First" flow and accesses the Local Vector Store (User Notes).

Fallback Response: "Looks like the cloud brain is sleeping (Network Error). Let's check your own notes while we wait. You wrote this about Integration last week..."

Benefit: Keeps the user in the app and studying, even during total service outage.

# **Addendum E: MAIT Technical & Pedagogical Refinements**

## **1\. Architectural Evolution: The "Hybrid Brain"**

The project has shifted from a theoretical cloud model to a **Hybrid Edge-Cloud Stack**, leveraging the latest 2025 capabilities of Gemini 3 Flash and WebGPU.

### **Layer 1 & 2: The "Edge" (Local Browser/Device)**

* **Engine:** Utilizing **WebLLM** and **Transformers.js** to run V-SLMs (Vision-Small Language Models) directly in the browser.  
* **Privacy Shield:** Implements local PII (Personally Identifiable Information) scrubbing. Names, school logos, and faces are redacted *on-device* before any data transits to the cloud.  
* **Local Truth:** Standard HSC formulas and basic algebraic OCR are handled locally to ensure sub-second response times.

### **Layer 3 & 4: The "Cloud Muscle" (Gemini 3 Flash)**

* **Role:** Acts as the **Verative Logic Layer**. It verifies complex 4-Unit integration/mechanics logic that SLMs might hallucinate.  
* **Orchestrated Latency:** While the cloud calculates the "Truth," the local UI engages the student with "Active Retrieval" tasks.

## **2\. Key Pedagogical Feature: "Active Retrieval Blur"**

To combat passive learning, MAIT will implement a **"Tap-to-Unblur" Formula Component**.

* **Mechanism:** Formulas required for a problem are rendered as SVGs with a CSS blur(12px) filter.  
* **Cognitive Load:** Forces "Shape Recognition" (System 1\) before revealing the full LaTeX (System 2).  
* **Gamification:** Students "tap" to reveal layers of the formula, reducing blur as they interact, shifting the experience from consumption to retrieval.

## **3\. Integration by Parts: The "Mentor" Explanation**

Moving beyond the "Reverse Product Rule" (Algebraic), the platform will offer **Geometric Intuition** as a "Deep Dive" mode.

* **The Area Proof:** Explaining $\\int u \\, dv \= uv \- \\int v \\, du$ as the subtraction of rectangular areas.  
* **Vibe-Switching:** \* *Biker Mode:* Shortcuts, LIATE mnemonic, exam-speed focus.  
  * *Mentor Mode:* Spatial reasoning, the "Why" behind the calculus, connecting math to mechatronics/physics.

## **4\. Implementation Strategy**

* **Primary API:** Gemini 3 Flash-Lite (optimized for low cost/high speed).  
* **Fallback Protocol:** If WebGPU is unavailable, the system triggers a **Consent-Based Cloud Fallback**, ensuring the student is aware and agrees to secure cloud processing.  
* **Zero-Persistence:** All cloud interactions are configured for ephemeral inference (no data retention for training).

# **ADDENDUM F: MAIT 3.0 — Always-On Multimodal Classroom AI**

**Date:** 12/05/2026 **Status:** Vision Lock — 2027-2028 Build Horizon. Do not begin engineering before pre-build conditions are met (see Phase 2). **Author:** Darayat Ilham Chowdhury

---

## **Founder Thesis**

**MAIT 3.0 is the EdTech I signed up for, minus the omniscience.**

The technical components for always-on, multimodal, per-student-tailored classroom AI exist as commodity by 2026\. Continuous transcription, real-time multimodal capture, per-student RAG, background generation — all shipping. The reason this configuration has not been deployed at scale is not capability. It is the absence of a credible trust architecture for capturing minors in real-time inside their own classrooms.

MAIT 3.0 is what happens when the right architecture finally catches up to the available capability.

## **Vision**

A continuous, multimodal classroom AI that:

* Captures classroom audio in real-time, on-premise only  
* Watches whiteboard and lesson visual content via dedicated camera  
* Tracks per-student engagement, comprehension, and contribution signals  
* Generates personalised homework in the background, ready before the bell  
* Produces parent-facing session summaries automatically, mediated through the school  
* Acts as the teacher's MKO and the student's Mate simultaneously, with full session context awareness  
* Closes the lesson-to-homework-to-next-lesson loop with no manual admin overhead

The teacher arrives at next session with summaries already written, homework already differentiated per student, and parent communications already drafted for review and approval.

## **The Ethical Foundation**

The default architecture for "AI that listens to classrooms" — audio streamed to cloud APIs, transcripts processed off-premise, data exhaust accessible to whichever vendor wrote the SDK — is regulatorily fragile, politically toxic, and ethically indefensible for minors in compulsory education.

MAIT 3.0 inverts this. The Hub-and-Spoke sovereign architecture (see April 2026 addendum) is not a feature. It is the **precondition**.

* **Audio of minors never leaves the school premises.**  
* **Transcription is local.**  
* **Summarisation is local.**  
* **Storage is local, audit-logged, and retention-bounded.**  
* **Parents see school-mediated summaries, never raw transcripts.**  
* **Vendor access to classroom data is structurally impossible by architectural design, not by policy promise.**

This is not a privacy policy. It is an architectural refusal.

## **Scope Refusals (What MAIT 3.0 Will Never Do)**

* Will not retain audio after on-device transcription  
* Will not stream classroom capture outside the school's physical premises under any circumstance  
* Will not enable cross-student surveillance or behavioural profiling  
* Will not enable administrator surveillance of teachers  
* Will not be marketed, framed, or sold as a "monitoring" or "compliance" tool  
* Will not integrate with disciplinary or HR workflows  
* Will not be sold to organisations whose use case is surveillance, regardless of price  
* Will not have a "see what the student said" feature in the parent portal

These are not policy commitments. They are product-level architectural decisions that make alternative uses technically impossible. The product physically cannot do these things, even if asked.

## **Trust Capital Sequencing**

MAIT 3.0 cannot ship until MAIT 1.0 and 2.0 have built the institutional credibility required to grant it permission to exist.

### **Phase 1 (Now → Q2 2027): MAIT 1.0/2.0 Ship and Adopt**

* Worksheet generator deployed and used at scale across multiple schools  
* Report comment agent and other teacher-side Copilot agents trusted in school workflows  
* Tutor-mediated student platform piloted with paying tutors and validated  
* Hub-and-Spoke proof-of-concept built at one institutional partner  
* 2+ year track record of zero privacy incidents under public scrutiny

### **Phase 2 (Q3 2027 → Q1 2028): Pre-Build Conditions**

All of the following must be met before engineering begins:

* NSW DoE classroom AI policy framework finalised and published  
* Federal AI Act position settled (if passed)  
* eSafety Commissioner guidance for AI in K-12 published  
* ACARA position on AI in classroom pedagogy clarified  
* One or more partner schools formally requesting MAIT 3.0 capability  
* Legal counsel retained on retainer  
* Data Protection Officer engaged  
* Senior engineering team of 3+ in place  
* Educational psychologist consultant retained  
* Independent privacy auditor identified

### **Phase 3 (2028+): Build and Pilot**

* 6-12 month build with security and privacy review at every stage  
* Pilot in 1-2 partner schools with full audit access for parents and DoE  
* Iterate based on real classroom telemetry  
* Scale to broader deployment only after pilot validation and third-party audit

## **Why Now-Building Would Fail**

Shipping any MAIT 3.0 prototype in 2026 is a mistake for four reasons:

1. **No school will permit always-on AI from an unknown vendor.** Trust must precede capability access. There is no shortcut.  
2. **The regulatory framework is still solidifying.** Building against draft rules means rebuilding when they finalise.  
3. **The first AI-in-classroom scandal is still pending.** Existing trusted vendors will weather it. New entrants will not. Be already trusted when it lands.  
4. **Solo-builder ceiling.** MAIT 3.0 requires team, legal, privacy expertise, and multi-disciplinary review. A vibe-coded MAIT 3.0 creates the scandal that ends the category for everyone.

The build moves to 2028 not because the vision is wrong, but because the conditions required for the vision to ship ethically have not yet matured. Patience here is the moat.

## **Technical Architecture (Draft — refine pre-Phase 3\)**

### **Capture Layer (On-Premise Edge)**

* Multi-microphone classroom array with voice-activity-detected local-only buffering  
* Optional whiteboard camera with local OCR pipeline  
* Per-student device-paired context capture (opt-in, parent-consented, encryption-at-rest)

### **Processing Layer (On-Premise Hub)**

* Local Whisper-class transcription, no cloud round-trip  
* Speaker diarisation and per-student tagging via voice fingerprinting  
* Engagement signal extraction (participation rate, question complexity, response latency)  
* Real-time RAG retrieval against syllabus and per-student context  
* Background generation queue for homework, summaries, parent communications

### **Output Layer (Multi-Channel)**

* Teacher dashboard: live engagement view, post-session summary, draft homework  
* Student companion app: personalised practice, scaffolded explanations, between-session continuity  
* Parent portal: school-mediated weekly summaries, no raw transcripts ever  
* Administrator audit log: read-only view of data flow, retention, and access

### **Governance Layer (Structural)**

* All processing on school-owned hardware, physically located within school premises  
* Cryptographic audit trail of every data access  
* Parent-facing data dashboard showing what was captured, what was generated, what was retained  
* Annual third-party privacy and security audit, results published  
* Bright-line architectural refusal of all secondary data use

## **Architectural Continuity**

MAIT 3.0 is the institutional-scale extension of the Aether Agent pattern: local autonomous compute, sovereign identity, structurally bounded data flow. The same architectural primitives that make Aether a personal operator make MAIT 3.0 an institutional one.

## **Founder's Note**

This addendum is written 36 hours after being invited onto the school's AI Committee, and 12 hours before contributing to a teacher-side report comment agent build. The work between now and MAIT 3.0 is not waiting — it is exactly the trust-building, infrastructure-deploying, regulatory-learning work that earns the right to ship MAIT 3.0 when the conditions are right.

The vision is locked. The path to it is the next two years of disciplined, ethical, deployed work, in service of schools that have not yet given me permission to build it.

**MAIT 3.0 ships when the school is ready to trust me with always-on. Not before. Not because of capability — because of integrity.**

# **Addendum 12 May ‘26 MAIT SafeView — Privacy-First Document Ingestion Summary**

## **Core Idea**

MAIT should treat **privacy-safe ingestion** as a default platform feature, not an optional add-on.

The system should allow teachers to upload or paste school material while automatically removing personally identifiable information before any cloud AI model processes it.

---

## **Main Principle**

Never send the original PDF/document/docx to the cloud.

Only send flattened, sanitised images or redacted text.

This avoids common PDF privacy failures such as:

* hidden text layers  
* embedded metadata  
* fake visual redaction  
* OCR leftovers  
* selectable text under black boxes  
* school logos or staff names remaining in headers  
* Author metadata

---

## 

## 

## **Recommended Pipeline**

Teacher uploads PDF / scan / image

↓

PDF is rasterised into page images

↓

Original PDF is immediately deleted

↓

Local redaction removes visible PII

↓

Local model checks for remaining risk

↓

Only sanitised images/text are sent to cloud AI

↓

Premium models are used only when needed

---

## **Why Vision Over OCR**

OCR is cheap and useful, but it is limited.

OCR is good for:

* printed text extraction  
* search/indexing  
* clean documents  
* basic forms

Vision is better for:

* handwritten student working  
* maths notation  
* diagrams  
* geometry  
* layout understanding  
* scanned worksheets  
* misconception diagnosis

For education, especially maths, **vision should be the default analysis mode** after sanitisation.

---

## **Pricing Summary**

Basic cloud OCR is very cheap:

\~$1–$2 per 1,000 pages

Cheap cloud vision can be surprisingly close in cost:

Gemini Flash-Lite / Flash ≈ $1–$5 per 1,000 pages

Premium vision/reasoning models are much more expensive:

Claude Sonnet / GPT-5.5 / Gemini Pro ≈ $12–$45+ per 1,000 pages

Therefore:

Use OCR for cheap extraction.

Use cheap vision for default document understanding.

Use premium models only for difficult reasoning or low-confidence cases.

---

## **Local Processing Layer**

Before any cloud request, MAIT should run local safeguards:

* regex removal of emails, phone numbers, IDs  
* known staff-name replacement  
* school-name and logo removal  
* header/footer redaction  
* metadata stripping  
* local OCR for rough PII detection  
* local NER/entity detection  
* local WebGPU/WebLLM model for risk checking

Possible local model stack:

* Gemma 4  
* Qwen  
* Phi  
* Mistral  
* Llama variants  
* Transformers.js  
* WebLLM/WebGPU

Local models should be used for:

redaction support, risk detection, routing, and verification

not as the only safety mechanism.

---

## 

## 

## 

## **Suggested Model Router**

Local deterministic redaction

↓

Local WebGPU/Gemma-style safety check

↓

Gemini Flash-Lite for cheap bulk vision

↓

Gemini Flash for normal worksheet/student-work analysis

↓

Claude Sonnet / GPT-5.5 / Gemini Pro only for hard escalation

---

## **Product Positioning**

This should be branded as a trust feature, for example:

* **MAIT SafeView**  
* **MAIT SafePaste**  
* **MAIT SafePDF**  
* **MAIT Privacy Layer**  
* **MAIT Safe Ingestion**

Teacher-facing copy:

Documents are protected locally before AI analysis.

Original PDFs are converted to images and discarded.

Names, logos, emails, and school identifiers are removed before processing.

---

## **Final Design Philosophy**

MAIT should not be “a chatbot that accepts school files.”

It should be:

An education-safe AI platform with privacy-by-default ingestion.

This creates a strong school-specific moat: safer than generic AI upload tools, better than brittle OCR workflows, and aligned with real teacher privacy concerns.

### **ADDENDUM G: The Metacognition & Resilience Engine**

**Date:** 13/05/2026 | **Status:** Active Strategic Direction

**Author/Architect:** Darayat Ilham Chowdhury

**1\. The Strategic Gap**

While the Artifact Generation Engine (A.G.E.) forces offline endurance, the live chat interface still risks creating passive consumers of information. If a student relies on the AI to bypass cognitive friction, we are failing the primary mission of the Mental Maths Mentor ethos: building resilience. We must codify the exact pedagogical boundaries the AI is allowed to operate within, ensuring it acts as a coach, not a calculator.

2\. Core Feature: The Socratic "Guide-Only" Protocol

* **Concept:** A hardcoded system prompt constraint that strictly prevents the AI from providing direct answers to syllabus-aligned problems.  
* **Mechanism:** The AI is locked into a coaching state. It is only permitted to ask guiding questions (e.g., "What do you think the first step is?"), offer targeted hints, or verify a mathematical solution *only after* the student has submitted a genuine attempt.  
* **Pedagogical Value:** Enforces Active Recall. It bridges the gap between the student's current ability and their potential by scaffolding the problem, mirroring the exact methodology used by elite human tutors.

3\. Core Feature: The "Feynman" Reverse-Tutoring Mode

* **Concept:** A flipped interaction state where the AI temporarily abandons the "Expert Mate" persona and simulates a novice student.  
* **Mechanism:** The AI intentionally injects common HSC mathematical misconceptions into the chat (e.g., forgetting the $+C$ in integration, or messing up the chain rule) and challenges the user to "teach" the concept back to it.  
* **Pedagogical Value:** Leverages the highest tier of Bloom's Taxonomy. It reinforces mastery through the "learning by teaching" method, forcing the student to articulate the *why* behind the mechanics.

4\. Core Feature: The Grit Tracker (Invisible Psychometrics)

* **Concept:** Shifting the analytics focus from "correctness" to "persistence."  
* **Mechanism:** The Local SLM monitors keystroke telemetry in the browser. If a student deletes and retypes an equation or sentence multiple times *before* hitting send, the system logs this as a high-friction metacognitive event.  
* **Outcome:** The system invisibly tracks this and triggers positive reinforcement from the Mate persona (e.g., "You worked through that yourself 💪").  
* **Stakeholder Value:** It rewards persistence, not just correctness. When integrated into the Tutor-Mediated dashboard, human educators can see exactly which students are fighting through the cognitive load and which ones are giving up, allowing for highly targeted emotional and academic interventions.

**5\. Implementation within the Tutor-Mediated Pivot**

These features are not universally active. Under the new B2B architecture, the human Tutor has granular control over these protocols via their dashboard. A tutor can dial the "Socratic strictness" up to 100% for a high-performing Extension 1 student, or lower it to provide more direct scaffolding for a Standard Maths student struggling with foundational confidence.

Claude Bars:

*"MAIT teacher-side agents operate as Vygotsky MKOs, not ghostwriters. Every output ends with a context-aware prompt that requires teacher pedagogical input — scaffolding the structure, requiring the seeing."*

The MAIT teacher-side stack uses upstream evidence guardrails combined with downstream MKO prompts to actively coach teachers back into professional pedagogical framing when their input is deficit-loaded or evidence-thin. In live stress testing, the prompt pack refused to produce a report comment for "bad kid, always hitting" — instead translating the behaviour into an Akhlaq value goal, pulling Year 4 curriculum vocabulary to scaffold the teacher's actual observation, and requiring the Input Template to proceed. This validates the design principle: 

**AI as MKO, not ghostwriter — protecting teacher craft by requiring teacher input, not replacing it.**

# **Tutor-Mediated Pivot**

# **Addendum: Tutor-Mediated Pivot**

**Date:** 9 May 2026   
**Author:** Darayat Ilham Chowdhury   
**Status:** Active strategic direction

---

## **Summary**

MAIT is repositioning from a direct-to-student AI tutor to a **tutor-mediated AI platform** where human teachers and tutors curate AI-powered learning experiences for their students. The core product loop is now Tutor → AI → Student, with the tutor remaining the pedagogical authority and the AI serving as the asynchronous bridge between sessions and the operational exoskeleton for the tutor's workflow.

The student-facing AI chat experience remains, but is contextualised through a tutor-configured account rather than offered as a standalone consumer product.

---

## **Why This Pivot Is Smart**

**1\. It matches what the founder has been doing manually for over a year.** The Custom Gem workflow with Mental Maths Mentor students is the manual version of this exact product. Productising the existing successful workflow is lower risk than inventing a new one.

**2\. It bypasses the institutional immune response.** Schools, AI Committees, parents, and teaching unions reflexively resist AI products framed as **replacing teachers**. Tutor-mediated AI is framed as **augmenting** them, which inverts the political calculus from threat to asset.

**3\. It cleanly avoids the dominant local competitor.** NSWEduChat is free, government-mandated, and being rolled out to every NSW public school student from Year 5+. Competing for that market is unwinnable. Independent schools, Catholic schools, and the entire private tutoring market are not served by NSWEduChat — and that's where MAIT wins.

**4\. It is structurally safer for minors.** The tutor relationship provides the human-in-the-loop oversight that has been missing in tragedies involving direct-to-student AI products. Concerning patterns surface to a real adult before they become crises.

**5\. The unit economics are cleaner.** A single buyer (the tutor) pays per-student, with student and parent access bundled in. No coordination problem of needing two parties to sign up and pay before the product works.

**6\. The first 50 customers are reachable.** The founder's existing tutoring network, Mental Maths Mentor brand, SLSO placement contacts, and B.Ed cohort are warm leads. No paid acquisition required for initial validation.

**7\. The market gap is genuinely empty.** No existing product combines tutor-side worksheet generation, student-tethered AI chat, structured progress dashboards, and NSW HSC syllabus depth. Closest comparables (Almanack, Edcafe AI, Khanmigo) each cover only one or two of those.

---

## **Roadmap**

### **Phase 1 — Dogfooding (4-8 weeks)**

* Continue using the manual Custom Gem workflow with existing Mental Maths Mentor students, explicitly framed as MAIT prototype testing  
* Build tutor-student tethering data model on top of existing MAIT codebase (Postgres now in place)  
* Implement JWT auth bound to Google OAuth  
* Add tutor account, student invitation, and basic dashboard  
* Replace Custom Gem workflow with MAIT proper for the founder's own students  
* Document everything: what students ask, where the gaps are, what the tutor needs to see

### **Phase 2 — Friendly Beta (8-16 weeks)**

* Onboard 3-5 friendly tutors (B.Ed cohort, Mental Maths Mentor colleagues) at $15-30/month per student tier  
* Add Stripe integration for subscriptions  
* Refine the tutor dashboard based on real usage  
* Build out the NSW HSC RAG corpus (NESA syllabus parsed into structured chunks with hybrid retrieval)  
* Implement the Dual-Agent Verification Circuit so pedagogical guardrails are enforced at scale  
* Stand up Cerberus autonomous adversarial testing on Aether (M1)

### **Phase 3 — Public Launch to Independent Tutors (16-24 weeks)**

* Launch publicly to Australian independent maths tutors  
* Marketing through Mental Maths Mentor brand, Instagram, Substack  
* Target 50-100 paying tutors by end of year  
* Refine product based on broader feedback

### **Phase 4 — Institutional Sales (24+ weeks)**

* Approach independent schools and Catholic schools with track record and case studies  
* The pending CEO meeting becomes a "here's how 50 tutors are already using this" pitch  
* Pilot agreements: one Year 12 maths class, one term, free in exchange for usage data and feedback rights  
* Position MAIT as the AI exoskeleton for entire maths faculties

### **Phase 5 — Adjacent Expansion (12-24 months)**

* Expand from Mathematics Advanced to Extension 1, Extension 2, Standard  
* Then to other HSC subjects from a position of credibility  
* Sovereign Hub-and-Spoke deployment option for schools that require on-premise data sovereignty  
* Eventually: parent-facing dashboards, group tutoring sessions, transcription, video features — only after core product is validated

---

## **What Carries Over From The Original Vision**

* **The "Mate" persona.** Australian English, Socratic, encouraging, never condescending. The voice doesn't change.  
* **NESA HSC syllabus alignment as the depth-of-coverage moat.** Going deep on NSW HSC Mathematics first, expanding outward.  
* **The wellness-first pedagogy.** Fatigue detection, Bloom's taxonomy progression, structured response format with core\_truth, explanation, hints. Now visible to tutors as well as informing the AI's behaviour.  
* **The Native Canvas LaTeX worksheet IDE.** Becomes the centrepiece of the tutor experience rather than a standalone teacher feature. Worksheets generated here become the topic anchors for student chat sessions.  
* **BYOK as one available pricing tier.** Repositioned for tutors who want to use their own Gemini API keys for cost control.  
* **The Glass Box transparency philosophy.** Honest about what the AI knows, what it doesn't, and what each interaction costs. Now extends to the tutor seeing the AI's reasoning, not just outputs.  
* **The Sovereign Hub-and-Spoke architecture.** Retained as the long-horizon enterprise destination for schools requiring on-premise deployment. Not Phase 1 work.  
* **The Dual-Agent Verification Circuit (Generator \+ Evaluator).** More important than ever — pedagogical guardrails must hold whether the tutor is watching or not.  
* **The CODEX identity framework.** The Architect/Sasquatch/Boy persona system continues to inform how the founder operates the build sustainably.  
* **The MyAITeam long-horizon vision.** Tutor-mediated AI for HSC students is the wedge into the broader thesis of personal, private, permanent AI companions for navigating the ASI transition. Same destination, clearer path.

---

## **New Features Introduced By This Pivot**

### **Tutor-Side Features**

* **Tutor account and dashboard.** Single source of truth for the tutor's students, sessions, and AI configurations.  
* **Student invitation flow.** Tutor adds students by name and parent email. Student receives access link tethered to the tutor's account.  
* **Per-student AI context configuration.** Tutor sets the syllabus scope, current focus topics, difficulty level, and pedagogical style for each student individually.  
* **Asynchronous activity dashboard.** Tutor sees what each student worked on between sessions, where they struggled, what topics need follow-up. Summary by default, full transcript on explicit request.  
* **Auto-generated lesson notes.** Hub LLM summarises the week's student-AI interactions into prep material for the next live session.  
* **NESA-aligned marking guidelines.** Auto-generated rubrics for the tutor's worksheets, in NSW conventions.

### **Student-Side Features (Tethered)**

* **Login via tutor invitation only.** No public student signup in v1.  
* **Tutor-curated chat context.** Mate already knows what topic the student is working on, what their current Bloom's level is, what they got wrong last session.  
* **Pedagogical guardrails configured by tutor.** The tutor decides how strictly Socratic Mate should be for each student.  
* **Optional after-hours access.** Configurable by the tutor and parent.

### **Parent-Side Features (Read-Only, Bundled)**

* **Sanitised progress reports.** Automated, weekly, framed in strength-based educator language.  
* **Visibility without surveillance.** Topic coverage and progress, not raw chat logs.

### **Infrastructure**

* **JWT auth bound to Google OAuth.** Replaces the IDOR-vulnerable header-matching approach.  
* **Multi-tenant Postgres schema.** Every relevant table includes tutor\_id for proper data isolation.  
* **NSW HSC RAG corpus.** Structured retrieval over NESA syllabus dot-points, replacing custom Gem keyword matching.  
* **Cerberus autonomous adversarial testing.** Nightly red-teaming runs ensuring pedagogical guardrails hold under pressure.

---

## **What's Explicitly Out Of Scope For Phase 1**

* Direct-to-consumer student signups without a tutor  
* Group tutoring features  
* Live video or audio sessions  
* Whiteboard or collaborative drawing  
* Parent-direct subscriptions (parent access bundled with tutor's subscription instead)  
* Mobile app (Phase 4+)  
* Sovereign Hub-and-Spoke on-premise deployment (Phase 5+)  
* Subjects beyond Mathematics Advanced  
* AI-generated video content  
* Marketplace or social features  
* Public API  
* Payment processing for tutor-to-parent billing (tutors handle their own client billing)

---

## **Strategic Positioning**

**One-line description:** MAIT is the AI exoskeleton for independent maths tutors and teachers in NSW, giving each student a tutor-curated AI study mate while saving tutors hours of administrative work per week.

**Why the world needs it:** AI in education is happening regardless of whether good builders ship good products. The choice is between students using ChatGPT alone in their bedrooms, NSWEduChat in classrooms with no human follow-up, or a tutor-mediated AI where the existing trust relationship between student and teacher is preserved and amplified. MAIT is the third option.

**Founder credibility:** Educator first, technologist second. B.Ed at Macquarie. Class Teacher of the Year 2023\. SLSO at independent school. Mental Maths Mentor brand. Building MAIT for himself before anyone else.

---

## **Next Concrete Action**

Continue dogfooding Mental Maths Mentor's existing students with the Custom Gem workflow as the manual MAIT prototype, while in parallel building the tutor-student tethering data model and dashboard in the actual MAIT codebase. Validate before scaling. Hold the broader vision as orientation, not as a deadline.

---

*This addendum supersedes the prior B2C-leaning framing while retaining the original vision document's pedagogical philosophy, technical architecture, and long-horizon ambition. The destination has not changed. The path to it has been clarified.*

**MAIT Wellness Integration \- Final Synthesis**

**1\. Tiered Support Surface (stolen from Anthropic tonight)**

* "Find resources" dropdown, not forced

**2\. Trigger Patterns (Keystroke Psychometrics)**

| Signal | Interpretation | Response |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Repeated delete-retype cycles WITHOUT sending | Frustration/stuck | Soft nudge: "Need a different approach?" |
| Long pauses \+ late hour \+ session length | Fatigue/struggling | "Take a breather? 🫁" |
| Rapid confident keystrokes → sudden stop | Hit a wall | Offer hint, not answer |
| Self-correction before AI help | GRIT \- reward this | Invisible tracker, positive reinforcement |
| Direct distress language | Crisis | Immediate Lifeline/Kids Helpline surface |

**3\. The Grit Tracker (your original insight)**

* Student deletes and retypes BEFORE sending \= metacognition  
* Track this invisibly  
* Reward persistence, not just correctness  
* "You worked through that yourself 💪" acknowledgment

**4\. Glass Box Transparency**

* Student KNOWS monitoring is happening  
* Consent-based, not surveillance  
* "MAIT notices when you're struggling and can offer help"  
* Optional parent/teacher flag for patterns over multiple sessions

**5\. Orchestrated Latency Integration**

* If wellness flag triggered, slow down AI response  
* Creates space for student to self-regulate  
* Not punitive \- protective

## **Memory and analytics engine from Claude**

\#\# MAIT Timetable & Analytics System

\#\#\# Core Concept  
A transparent, user-controlled data management system inspired by Claude's memory architecture. Users can view, add, remove, and replace entries using simple commands, creating trust through visibility while enabling powerful analytics.

\#\#\# Student-Facing Features

\*\*Timetable Management\*\*  
\- View: Display current study schedule, upcoming sessions, exam dates  
\- Add: "Add exam: Physics, March 15" / "Add tutoring session Thursday 4pm"  
\- Remove: Delete completed or cancelled entries by line number  
\- Replace: Reschedule sessions without losing history ("Replace \#3 → Friday 5pm")

\*\*Progress Tracking\*\*  
\- Numbered entries for topics covered, milestones hit, areas of difficulty  
\- Students see exactly what the system "knows" about their learning journey  
\- No black-box algorithms — full transparency on how insights are generated

\#\#\# Tutor/Analytics Side

\*\*Session Intelligence\*\*  
\- Automatic logging of session history, topics covered, time spent  
\- Engagement metrics derived from keystroke psychometrics (typing speed, pause patterns, correction frequency)  
\- Flagging system: "This student's engagement dropped 40% over last 2 weeks"

\*\*Wellness Monitoring Integration\*\*  
\- Behavioural signals feed into wellness flags (not just academic performance)  
\- Parents/guardians can see \*why\* a flag was raised, not just that it exists  
\- Configurable alert thresholds per student

\#\#\# UX Principles

1\. \*\*Numbered entries\*\* \= scannable, not overwhelming  
2\. \*\*Command-based interface\*\* (view/add/remove/replace) \= simple mental model anyone can learn  
3\. \*\*Full visibility\*\* \= trust \+ transparency (users see what the AI "knows")  
4\. \*\*No black boxes\*\* \= wellness flags explain their reasoning

\#\#\# Differentiation  
Unlike generic scheduling apps, this system creates a feedback loop between timetable adherence, engagement data, and wellness signals — all visible to the appropriate stakeholders (student, tutor, parent) at their permission level.

### **MAIT Feature Expansion: The "Friction & Authenticity" Update**

**1\. Dynamic Fatigue Lockout (The "Cognitive CAPTCHA")**

* **Concept:** Transitioning from a rigid screen-time penalty to a dynamic cognitive assessment to prevent AI over-reliance.  
* **Mechanism:** When the system detects high session length or specific fatigue markers, the AI persona initiates a "Proof of Energy" challenge (e.g., a targeted, high-friction question based on the immediate study session).  
* **Outcome:** A correct answer grants a session extension, proving the student's working memory and cognitive load can handle more input. An incorrect answer, guess, or bypass triggers the temporary hard lockout.  
* **Pedagogical Value:** Enforces active retrieval practice and ensures the system acts as a cognitive safety net rather than a crutch.

**2\. Auto-Dim Idle Tracker (The Authenticity Metric)**

* **Concept:** Eliminating vanity metrics and the "fake studying" loophole (leaving a tab open to inflate study hours).  
* **Mechanism:** The UI detects idle mouse movement, lack of keystrokes, or tab-away events. Upon detection, the screen progressively dims (after 1 minute of no activity) and the active study timer is paused. The UI restores and the timer resumes only upon physical interaction.  
* **Outcome:** Ensures the system generates a 100% authentic Engagement Efficiency Score (EES).  
* **Stakeholder Value:** When parents and teachers review the Google Sheets telemetry dashboard, they see data reflecting genuine, high-friction cognitive work, establishing absolute trust in the platform's reporting.  
* Works even when they switch to YouTube or another tab so the time on app is still accurate.

**3\. The "Offline Loop" Workflow (Digital-to-Physical Bridge)**

* **Concept:** Acknowledging the physical reality of traditional pen-and-paper examinations (e.g., the HSC) by forcing a digital disconnect.  
* **Mechanism:** 1\. **Engage:** The student uses MAIT to review topics and trigger the Artifact Generation Engine (A.G.E.) to create a custom, compiled PDF worksheet.  
  2\. **Disconnect:** MAIT initiates a "Printer Mode" temporary lockout, forcing the student off the device to complete the mathematical or written work manually.  
  3\. **Reconnect:** The student returns to the platform, the lockout lifts, and the AI is used to verify handwritten answers, log mistakes, and provide targeted feedback.  
* **Pedagogical Value:** Drastically reduces total screen time, builds independent test-taking stamina, and neutralizes institutional fears regarding "screen addiction."

### **Proposed Amendment to MAIT Vision Document (v2.1)**

**Addendum Section: The Artifact Generation Engine (A.G.E.)**

#### **1\. The Strategic Gap**

Current EdTech has a fatal flaw: **The Medium Mismatch.**

* **The Reality:** The HSC is a pen-and-paper examination requiring endurance, handwriting speed, and geometrical precision.  
* **The Gap:** MAIT’s current vision optimizes *digital* learning but risks creating "iPad Kids" who falter when handed a physical booklet.  
* **The Opportunity:** We can turn the "Mandatory Break" (Pillar 3\) from a passive lockout into an active "Offline Simulation."

#### **2\. Core Feature: The Artifact Generation Engine**

**Definition:** A dedicated microservice that converts AI-generated logic into professional, NESA-styled, printable PDF assets (Artifacts) on demand.

**The Workflow:**

1. **Trigger:** Student hits "Generate Mock Exam" OR the "Wellness Engine" detects 2 hours of screen time.  
2. **Generation:** The AI selects tailored questions based on weak spots (Pillar 1).  
3. **Compilation:** The system compiles a .tex file into a PDF in real-time, including vector diagrams (TikZ) for geometry/calculus.  
4. **Action:** The App locks the digital interface and displays a countdown: *"Printer mode active. Complete this 20-minute paper. See you on the other side."*

#### **3\. Key Capabilities**

* **Vector-Perfect Diagrams:** Unlike competitors who paste low-res JPEGs, A.G.E. generates math-perfect coordinate systems, triangles, and physics diagrams using code. They never pixelate when printed.  
* **The "Exam Room" Simulator:** The generated PDF mimics the exact font (Arial/Helvetica), layout, and "End of Paper" styling of official NESA HSC examinations. This builds psychological familiarity.  
* **Tutor-Grade Answer Keys:** A separate "Marker's Guidelines" PDF is generated simultaneously, allowing the student (or parent) to self-mark with strict criteria.

#### **4\. Technical Architecture (The "Vibe Code" Spec)**

* **Input:** JSON Object from RAG (Question Data).  
* **Processor:** LaTeX Template Injection (injects the "Universal Preamble").  
* **Compiler:** Serverless Docker Container (AWS Lambda) running a lightweight TeX distribution (e.g., Tectonic).  
* **Output:** Ephemeral S3 Link (Auto-deletes after 24 hours to save storage).

#### **5\. Business Impact ("The Moat" Expansion)**

* **Parental Buy-In:** "MyAlTutor is the only app that tells my kid to get *off* the screen and do real work."  
* **The "Teacher Killer" Feature (B2B):** Teachers spend 10+ hours a week formatting worksheets. MAIT does it in 10 seconds. This feature alone justifies the B2B licensing cost.

**Phase 1: The Hook & The Traction (0 \- 45 seconds)** "Thank you for the time. You likely know me as the new SLSO, but my background is actually in Mechatronics and Computer Science from UNSW. I pivoted to Education because I saw a massive gap in how we support both teachers and students.

Right now, teachers spend hours fighting with formatting and lesson prep. Students burn out because standard digital tools don't recognize when they are hitting a cognitive wall.

To solve the first problem, I built a zero-cost, hyper-specific AI worksheet generator. Your Deputy Principal and several of your teachers are already using it right now to instantly generate NESA-aligned, compile-ready LaTeX math worksheets. I solved their formatting tax in 3 seconds. But that is just step one."\*

**Phase 2: The Vision & The Differentiator (45 \- 120 seconds)** \*"The main project is MAIT—My AI Tutor. It is a dedicated platform for HSC Maths.

The problem with slapping a standard LLM in front of a student is that it just gives them the answer, or it overwhelms them. MAIT uses a proprietary 'Tri-Brain' architecture that is **fatigue-aware**. It actively monitors typing cadence and delete-retype cycles to detect cognitive fatigue.

But it goes a step further to solve a problem every school faces: **Vanity Metrics**. Every major EdTech platform sells schools on 'time-on-screen.' As a teacher, I know that usually just means a student left the tab open while scrolling TikTok on their phone.

To combat this, I engineered an *Active Cognitive Engagement* filter into MAIT's UI. If the system detects a lack of physical input—no mouse movement, no typing, no scrolling—it assumes the student has disconnected and slowly dims the interface to 25% opacity, just like a laptop going to sleep. The moment they engage, it instantly wakes up.

We stop tracking empty screen time and start tracking actual, focused learning. And because it’s built by an educator, the timer is context-dependent. If the AI asks a quick mental maths question, the screen dims after 30 seconds of inactivity to push the pace. If it generates a complex calculus explanation, it gives them three minutes to read and process. It’s a frictionless way to measure real ROI without any of the ‘vanity metrics’.

**Phase 3: The Proof & The Ask (120 \- 180 seconds)** \*"I have the pedagogical proof: I won Class Teacher of the Year at one of Sydney's largest tutoring companies. I have the technical proof: your own staff are currently using my MVP to save hours of prep time.

I’m looking to the future. As I build out the student-facing MAIT platform for a 2026 launch, I want this school to be at the forefront. My ask is simple: I would love your blessing to continue refining these AI tools alongside your teaching staff, with the goal of running an official, controlled pilot of the MAIT student platform here when it’s ready.

I want to help build a system that supports your teachers' workload and protects your students' cognitive health.

# **MAIT: The Sovereign Educational AI**

### **Executive Proposal: Engineering High-Fidelity Resilience**

**Vision:** To provide every student with curriculum-aligned AI learning systems that prioritise mental growth and holistic well-being. We don’t just teach mathematics; we teach survival logic.

## **1\. The Institutional Bottleneck**

Schools in NSW are facing a three-front crisis in the age of generative AI:

1. **Data Sovereignty Liabilities:** Generic wrappers (like ChatGPT) expose schools to severe child-protection risks when students input Personally Identifiable Information.  
2. **Structural Teacher Burnout:** Senior Mathematics educators burn 10+ hours weekly on low-leverage, administrative formatting for NESA-aligned worksheets.  
3. **The "Vanity Metric" Trap:** Traditional EdTech optimizes for "time-on-screen." Schools are paying for software where students leave tabs open while scrolling their phones.

## **2\. The Architecture of Leverage**

MAIT treats the student's mind as a system to be optimized. It is a **Sovereign Educational AI platform** engineered for the HSC context, balancing elite compute with absolute data privacy.

### **The "Privacy Airlock" (Tri-Brain Architecture)**

MAIT runs a Small Language Model (SLM) *locally* on the student's device. This edge-compute layer acts as an aggressive firewall. It utilizes local `Regex` and OCR to scrub names, locations, and PII *before* interfacing with the secure Cloud LLM. **Zero sensitive data leaves the browser.**

### **The Universal Worksheet/Artifact Generator**

A microservice that compiles curriculum-locked, differentiated PDF worksheets based on live telemetry. It renders complex `TikZ` geometric diagrams, circuit schematics, and NESA-styled answer keys in seconds.

**The Problem:** Traditional worksheet creation for specific syllabus outcomes (Units/Estimation) usually takes a teacher 15–30 minutes of searching, formatting, and adjusting difficulty levels.

**The Execution:** Using MAIT, the Year 2 teacher accessed the platform via her own device. With five clicks, the architecture bypassed the local connectivity bottleneck.  A 2-page, pedagogical artifact—complete with diagrams and a full Teacher Answer Key— printed in \< 60s

## **3\. The Proactive Wellness Engine & Pedagogical Rigor**

MAIT is engineered to enforce high-friction cognitive work while drastically lowering the activation energy required to start studying.

* **UI Camouflage (The "Snap" Interface):** We abandon clunky LMS aesthetics for an interface mimicking iMessage. This reduces cognitive load and removes the friction of starting a study session.  
* **Orchestrated Latency ("Guess-First" Protocol):** MAIT kills the spinning loading wheel. It uses the 3-second `API` processing time to force Active Recall: “*That’s a complex problem. While I prepare the solution, what’s your first instinct for the starting step?”*  
* **The Opacity Filter (Killing Vanity Metrics):** If the UI detects a lack of physical input (e.g., the student tabs away to YouTube), the screen actively dims and the study timer pauses, varied depending on the context. MAIT generates a true **Engagement Efficiency Score (EES)**—giving executives telemetry they can actually trust.  
* **Dynamic Fatigue Lockouts:** By monitoring typing cadence and delete-retype cycles, MAIT detects cognitive exhaustion. It triggers mandatory 20-20-20 rule breaks and initiates **‘Touch Grass Mode’**, pushing the student offline to take a break.

## **4\. Equitable Deployment: The "BYOK" Infrastructure**

MAIT operates on a highly scalable, equitable deployment model designed to minimize institutional overhead.

* **The BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) "Totally-Free" Tier:** Schools or students can plug in their own secure `API` keys. This grants access to the elite pedagogical engine at zero compute cost to our servers, ensuring 100% free access for disadvantaged cohorts.  
* **The Freemium Friction:** Users without keys access the free tier, which includes extended mandatory wellness lockouts (e.g., a 5-minute forced break every 25 minutes, mirroring the Pomodoro Technique). Upgrading buys uninterrupted "flow state" processing, directly aligning the business model with healthy pedagogy.

% QUESTION 18 (Calculus \- Trapezoidal Rule)  
\\item \\textbf{Calculus (Numerical Integration):} The diagram below shows the curve $y \= \-\\frac{1}{2}x^3 \+ 3x^2 \- \\frac{9}{2}x \+ 4$. Use the Trapezoidal Rule with 4 subintervals to find an approximation for the area bounded by the curve, the $x$-axis, and the lines $x=0$ and $x=4$. \\hfill\\quad\\mbox{\\textbf{\[3 Marks\]}}

\\vspace{0.1cm}  
\\textit{$\\bm{\\int\_{a}^{b} f(x) \\, dx \\approx \\frac{h}{2} \\left\[ f(a) \+ 2 \\sum\_{i=1}^{n-1} f(x\_i) \+ f(b) \\right\]}$}

\\begin{center}  
\\begin{tikzpicture}  
\\begin{axis}\[  
    axis lines=middle, xmin=-0.5, xmax=5, ymin=-0.5, ymax=6,  
    xtick={0, 1, 2, 3, 4}, ytick={2, 3, 4},  
    width=8cm, height=6.5cm, tick label style={font=\\scriptsize}, clip=false  
\]  
    % Draw the solid trapezoids  
    \\draw\[fill=blue\!10, draw=black, thick\] (axis cs:0,0) \-- (axis cs:0,4) \-- (axis cs:1,2) \-- (axis cs:1,0) \-- cycle;  
    \\draw\[fill=blue\!10, draw=black, thick\] (axis cs:1,0) \-- (axis cs:1,2) \-- (axis cs:2,3) \-- (axis cs:2,0) \-- cycle;  
    \\draw\[fill=blue\!10, draw=black, thick\] (axis cs:2,0) \-- (axis cs:2,3) \-- (axis cs:3,4) \-- (axis cs:3,0) \-- cycle;  
    \\draw\[fill=blue\!10, draw=black, thick\] (axis cs:3,0) \-- (axis cs:3,4) \-- (axis cs:4,2) \-- (axis cs:4,0) \-- cycle;

    % Plot the actual curve over the top

\\textbf{Q1: Measurement} \\\\

\\textbf{Q2: Trigonometry} \\\\  
$\\tan(42^\\circ) \= \\frac{h}{15}$ \\\\  
$h \= 15 \\times \\tan(42^\\circ) \\approx 13.51$ m.

\\textbf{Q3: Optimization} \\\\  
By similar triangles: $\\frac{h}{H} \= \\frac{R-r}{R} \\implies h \= H\\left(1 \- \\frac{r}{R}\\right)$. \\\\  
$V \= \\pi r^2 H\\left(1 \- \\frac{r}{R}\\right)$. \\\\  
$\\frac{dV}{dr} \= \\pi H \\left(2r \- \\frac{3r^2}{R}\\right) \= 0 \\implies r \= \\frac{2}{3}R$. \\\\  
$h \= \\frac{1}{3}H$. Max Vol $= \\frac{4}{27}\\pi R^2 H$.

\\textbf{Q4: RLC Circuit} \\\\  
$f\_r \= \\frac{1}{2\\pi\\sqrt{LC}}$. $L \= 20 \\times 10^{-3}$ H, $C \= 50 \\times 10^{-6}$ F. \\\\  
$f\_r \= \\frac{1}{2\\pi \\times 10^{-3}} \= \\frac{1000}{2\\pi} \\approx 159.15$ Hz.

\\textbf{Q5: Chemistry} \\\\  
Groups: Carboxyl (carboxylic acid), Ester, Aromatic (benzene) ring. \\\\  
Eq: $\\ce{C7H6O3 \+ C4H6O3 \-\> C9H8O4 \+ C2H4O2}$

\\textbf{Q6: Time} \\\\  
12-hour: 10:10 AM. 24-hour: 10:10.

\\textbf{Q7: Surface Area Net} \\\\  
Rectangles: $(10\\times3) \+ (10\\times4) \+ (10\\times5) \= 120$ cm$^2$. \\\\  
Triangles: $2 \\times (\\frac{1}{2} \\times 3 \\times 4\) \= 12$ cm$^2$. \\\\  
Total SA $= 132$ cm$^2$.

\\textbf{Q8: Direction Field} \\\\  
Solution curve passes through $(0,1)$, moves downwards to the right (negative gradient), and eventually becomes asymptotic to the line $y \= x \- 1$.

\\textbf{Q9: Trig Graphing} \\\\  
Standard sine wave properties: Amplitude \= 2, vertical shift \= \+1. Range is $\[-1, 3\]$. Curve starts at $(0,1)$, peaks at $(\\frac{\\pi}{2}, 3)$, crosses axis at $\\pi$, troughs at $(\\frac{3\\pi}{2}, \-1)$.

\\textbf{Q10: 3D Vectors} \\\\  
$\\mathbf{u} \\cdot \\mathbf{v} \= (4)(0) \+ (4)(3) \+ (2)(4) \= 20$. \\\\  
$|\\mathbf{u}| \= 6$, $|\\mathbf{v}| \= 5$. \\\\  
$\\cos\\theta \= \\frac{20}{30} \\implies \\theta \\approx 48^\\circ$.

\\textbf{Q11: Complex Roots} \\\\  
Roots are solutions to $z^5 \- 1 \= 0$. \\\\  
Geometric sum $S\_5 \= \\frac{1(1-w^5)}{1-w}$. \\\\  
Since $w^5 \= 1$, sum is 0\.

\\textbf{Q12: Circle Geometry} \\\\

\\textbf{Q13: Statistics} \\\\  
Sum of probabilities $= 1 \\implies 3k \+ 0.55 \= 1 \\implies k \= 0.15$. \\\\  
$E(X) \= (0)(0.1) \+ (1)(0.3) \+ (2)(0.3) \+ (3)(0.15) \+ (4)(0.15) \= 1.95$.

\\textbf{Q14: Algorithmic Recursion} \\\\  
$a\_1 \= 3 \\implies a\_2 \= 5 \\implies a\_3 \= 9 \\implies a\_4 \= 17$.

\\textbf{Q18: Numerical Integration (Trapezoidal Rule)} \\\\  
$h \= \\frac{4-0}{4} \= 1$ \\\\  
Function values: $f(0)=1$, $f(1)=1.5$, $f(2)=3$, $f(3)=5.5$, $f(4)=9$ \\\\
